# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 26 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_026_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 26

**1** Jesus said: "You see the splinter [хов] that is in your brother's eye [вал], but you do not see the log [шоіт] that is in your own eye [вал].

**2** When you cast the log out of your own eye, then you will see clearly [оуонх] to cast the splinter [хов] out of your brother's eye."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *хов*: splinter, chip, mote — a small piece of wood or debris in the eye
- *шоіт*: beam, rafter, log — the large piece of wood; the contrast is extreme
- The Greek parallel: P.Oxy 1 lines 1-4 preserves this saying in nearly identical form
- cf. Matt 7:3-5; Luke 6:41-42 — nearly verbatim Synoptic parallels
- This is among the sayings most closely aligned with the Synoptic tradition
- The saying is pure criticism of hypocritical judgment
